claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me **how many children you're responsible for and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here in Birmingham.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is 17 and lives with you in Birmingham.

Since Alex is 16 or over, there are some additional eligibility requirements. Could you please tell me: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he attending school, college, university, or doing an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He recently left school actually. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next - whether that's college, work, or something else. He's been working with them for a few weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great news! The fact that Alex has registered with the local careers service is an important detail.

Before I can give you a final answer, I need to clarify one more thing: **When exactly did Alex leave school?** Specifically, how many weeks ago did he leave?

This matters because there's a 20-week window for continuing Child Benefit when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a careers service.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school about 12 weeks ago. So he's been out of school for roughly three months now, and he registered with the careers service shortly after leaving.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He left school approximately 12 weeks ago
- He registered with the local careers service shortly after leaving school
- He lives with you in Birmingham

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex registered with the careers service and it's only been 12 weeks, he is still within the 20-week eligibility window.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though he's 17 and has left school, he qualifies for a 20-week continuation period because he registered with the local careers service. Since he's only been out of school for 12 weeks, he's well within that 20-week window. This means you can claim Child Benefit for him now.

If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
